habit_scope: FM 5-426 Ch7: an underlay of ROOFING FELT is first applied to the sheathing before asphalt. Technique not code. Not AF&PA floor underlayment (txt 77/995). Not Logan ice barrier (that is MarketNote mn-logan). Not a Fontana snow pack. Do not invent IRC R905.
how_it_is_done: Deck on, swept, dry, no holes (FM: no roofing unless sheathing boards are absolutely dry).

FM 5-426: an underlay of roofing felt is first applied to the sheathing. Roofing felt usually comes in 3-foot-wide rolls and should be laid with a 2-inch top lap and a 4-inch side lap. Then starter course / asphalt strips. This is the sourced ROOF felt layout. Technique not code. Confirm AHJ.
AF&PA 'Underlayment' in the flooring chapter (txt 77 TOC / 995) is FLOOR underlayment under resilient tile/carpet — do not file it as roof felt.

AF&PA Type 15 asphalt felt: (1) 18-in underlay between wood-shake courses, or solid sheathing + Type 15 under shakes where wind-driven snow is encountered; (2) siding underlay. Those are not this asphalt-shingle underlay method.

HUD: ASTM D1970 named as self-adhering underlayment for a sealed roof deck — minimum 4-inch-wide strips over sheathing joints in hurricane/high-wind guidance. IRC high-wind underlayment ASTM D226 Type II (30 lb) named in that same HUD high-wind paragraph. That is hurricane/high-wind CLASS, not Fontana habit and not a national ice layout. ASTM D1970 title also names ice-dam protection — spec name only, not a field layout and not IRC R905.

CMHC eave protection (printed 138-139, Fig 100) is Canadian NBC: membrane along the eave under the starter; self-adhering bituminous or roll roofing; at least 900 mm (36 in) up the slope to a point at least 300 mm (12 in) inside the inner face of the exterior wall; not required on unheated garages/porches, slope 1:1.5 or greater, or regions with 3500 or fewer HDD. Label: Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do NOT copy onto Fontana. Logan ice barrier is on the CITY SHEET (mn-logan), not this Method and not these dimensions unless the AHJ says so.
Cover without delay after the deck (CMHC; AF&PA). Shingles themselves are P11 roof finish, not this dry-in Method.

tools_equipment: FM: scaffold to eaves about waist-high. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: Sheathing dry and inspected before felt (FM).
Roofing felt 3-ft rolls, 2-in top lap, 4-in side lap (FM). Technique not code — confirm AHJ.
Do not treat AF&PA floor underlayment as this layer.
Do not treat Logan ice barrier as this Method (mn-logan city sheet).
Do not walk CMHC 36 in / 12 in eave protection onto Fontana (Canadian / not IRC).
material_classes: self-adhering bituminous membrane CLASS (CMHC eave / HUD D1970 high-wind — not Fontana habit, not Logan city-sheet substitute)
when_this_beats_habit: This is the dry-in felt step the Army book names before asphalt. Ice barrier is a separate MarketNote on the Logan city sheet, not a cheaper skip of this felt and not a Fontana add.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Filing AF&PA floor underlayment as roof felt. Inventing IRC R905. Shopping ice barrier as Fontana habit. Using HUD 4-in D1970 strips as Wasatch/Fontana habit (high-wind CLASS).
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They roll felt. What they skip is that the only sourced lap numbers in these five books are FM 2-in top / 4-in side — technique not code — and ice is the city sheet, not a national habit.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Underlayment / ice barrier when the AHJ requires it (Logan city sheet). Confirm with AHJ / engineer. Do not invent R905. No stamp.
risk_if_swapped_late: Skipping felt until after occupancy is a leak, not a save. Ice on a Fontana takeoff is the wrong climate.
plain_language_summary: Once the deck is on, roll roofing felt before the shingles. The Army book is the one that actually names roof felt: 3-foot rolls, 2-inch top lap, 4-inch side lap. That is technique, not the IRC. The AF&PA 'underlayment' chapter is the floor. Logan ice barrier is on the city sheet — do not put a Utah ice pack on a Fontana roof.
spanish_summary: Con el forro puesto, el felt de techo va antes de las tejas. El libro del ejercito es el que nombra felt de techo: rollos de 3 pies, traslape de 2 pulgadas arriba y 4 a los lados. Es tecnica, no el IRC. El 'underlayment' de AF&PA es de piso. La barrera de hielo de Logan esta en la hoja de la ciudad — no ponga nieve de Utah en un techo de Fontana.
